items.title: Austria weighs military service reform
items.gist: Talks on changing military service have made some progress. But the government has not yet reached a deal.
items.summary: Austria’s governing parties held talks on reforming military service. The Ö1 evening news reported some optimism after the negotiations. The parties have not announced a final agreement. The debate concerns how Austria should organise its armed forces and service system. The latest report did not give details of a settled plan.
items.host_open: Austria is still working out what service should look like. How do you feel about the debate?

items.title: Austria plans higher truck tolls
items.gist: Using Austrian motorways will cost freight firms more next year. The increase is linked partly to road costs and emissions.
items.summary: Austria has published its truck toll rules for 2027. The increase will range from three to 3.6 percent, depending on the vehicle. Infrastructure and CO2 charges will rise by 3.6 percent. Charges for noise and air pollution will stay unchanged. Transport groups say Austria already has the EU’s highest tolls, while the Chamber of Labour has argued for higher charges to limit transit traffic.
items.host_open: The motorway bill for trucks is heading up. How does that look from Austria?

items.title: Austria pension costs keep rising
items.gist: State support for Austria’s pension system is forecast to grow in coming years. The increase is expected to be slower than before.
items.summary: Austria’s Pension Commission released a medium-term forecast. Federal support for the statutory pension system is expected to rise through 2031. The forecast says spending will reach about 27 billion euros by then. The increase is expected to be slower than in earlier years. The figures matter for future budget planning and debate over pensions.
items.host_open: Pension forecasts are a reminder that budgets have long memories. What did you make of the figures?

items.title: Germany passes its 2027 budget
items.gist: The Bundestag has approved the federal spending plan for next year. Opposition parties criticised both the budget and how it was prepared.
items.summary: Germany’s Bundestag approved the 2027 federal budget on Friday. The governing coalition of the CDU, CSU and SPD backed it. The vote was 317 in favour and 260 against. Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil described the budget as challenging and said further savings would be needed in 2028. Opposition members criticised the plan and the late changes made during its preparation.
items.host_open: Germany’s budget cleared parliament after a difficult debate. Did that surprise you?

items.title: EU budget talks end without a deal
items.gist: A summit on the next EU budget ended early without agreement. Leaders now face more negotiations over how the bloc should spend its money.
items.summary: An EU summit on the bloc’s budget ended early without a deal. The talks concerned the EU’s long-term spending plans. Austria’s Chancellor Christian Stocker called for careful spending. The budget debate involves competing demands from member states and different policy priorities. The summit’s early end means negotiations will have to continue.
items.host_open: The EU budget meeting ended before the numbers did. How does that look from Austria?

items.title: Zelenskyy urges US pressure on Russia
items.gist: Ukraine’s president called for stronger US pressure on Moscow. He also questioned Donald Trump’s description of Vladimir Putin as a friend.
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged the United States to put pressure on Russia. In a BBC interview, he questioned Trump’s description of Putin as a friend. The remarks come as Russia continues attacks on Ukraine. Kyiv says stronger pressure is needed to help end the war on acceptable terms. Moscow has not agreed to Ukraine’s demands for ending the conflict.
items.host_open: Diplomacy is hard to separate from trust in wartime. How did Zelenskyy’s message strike you?

items.title: Israeli strikes kill people in Gaza
items.gist: Reports say Israeli attacks killed people in Gaza this week. The violence continues despite a ceasefire agreement reached last year.
items.summary: Israeli strikes killed people in Gaza, according to reports published this week. The attacks took place despite a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas that began in October 2025. Gaza’s Health Ministry reported the deaths. Israel has said it targets Hamas and has accused the group of operating within civilian areas. The continued violence raises concern about the durability of the ceasefire and the safety of civilians.
items.host_open: The ceasefire has not ended the danger for people in Gaza. How are you feeling about the latest reports?

items.title: Houthi reports deaths after Yemen strikes
items.gist: The Houthi movement says Saudi airstrikes killed at least eleven people in Yemen. The reported toll and circumstances have not been independently confirmed in the available account.
items.summary: Houthi officials said Saudi aircraft struck a building in Yemen’s Taiz province. Their news agency reported at least eleven deaths, many of them children. The group said some people were still missing and rescue work was difficult. The reported account came from media controlled by the Houthis. The claims could not be independently confirmed in the available report.
items.host_open: Reports of children among the dead are deeply troubling. How are you processing the news?

items.title: Foodora sale agreed to avoid competition concerns
items.gist: Delivery Hero plans to sell foodora’s business in Austria and other countries. The buyer is a New York investment firm, with a loan from Uber to fund the purchase.
items.summary: Delivery Hero agreed to sell businesses in 14 countries, including foodora in Austria. The buyer is investment firm SSW Partners, based in New York. The agreed price is 1.4 billion euros. Uber will provide a loan covering the full purchase price. The companies expect the deal to close in the second half of 2027, subject to the remaining steps.
items.host_open: Food delivery is changing hands across several countries. Did that surprise you?

items.title: Austria’s army bars some electric cars
items.gist: Austria’s military plans to ban cars made by Chinese companies and Tesla from its sites. The decision was reported by ORF television.
items.summary: Austria’s armed forces plan to prohibit cars made by Chinese companies and Tesla from military sites. ORF reported the planned restriction on Friday. The report did not provide full details of how the rule will be applied. The decision concerns vehicles from companies with links to China and the US. The military has not published a full explanation in the available report.
items.host_open: A car park can become a security question surprisingly quickly. What do you think of that rule?

items.title: New fly species found in Vienna
items.gist: Researchers have discovered a previously unknown fly species at Vienna’s Natural History Museum. The find adds a small but notable piece to the record of local biodiversity.
items.summary: A new species of fly was discovered at the Natural History Museum in Vienna. ORF included the finding in its Friday evening news list. The discovery was made by researchers studying specimens and species. The available report did not give the fly’s scientific name or detailed habitat. New species records help scientists understand biodiversity and how it is documented.
items.host_open: Even a museum collection can still hold surprises. Did you expect a new species to turn up in Vienna?

items.title: Thanksgiving parade goes ahead in New York
items.gist: Organisers say the postponed 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving parade will still take place. The revised show includes LL Cool J and Gloria Gaynor.
items.summary: The organisers of New York’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade said the event would go ahead after being postponed. The parade is marking its 100th edition. Executive producer Will Coss said the organisers would deliver the show they had planned. The revised lineup includes LL Cool J and Gloria Gaynor. The original lineup included other performers, including Jimmy Fallon and The Roots.
items.host_open: A century-old parade has had to adjust its plans. Did the new lineup catch your eye?
